title: it-novum and publicplan are both Allgeier SE subsidiaries, so two list rows share a parent
content:
it-novum GmbH is an Allgeier SE subsidiary, and so is publicplan GmbH, which already sits on the same lead list. That is the finding: two rows in the corpus are one corporate group, so the apparent count of independent German public-sector leads is overstated by one.

Group ownership cuts both ways here. It means the two rows will share alliance frameworks, procurement standards and possibly delivery decisions, so an approach to one is partly an approach to both, and a rejection at group level could close both at once. It also means an opening at either subsidiary is a route into the other — the same handling logic recorded for Conclusion's federation of operating companies, where the instruction is to sell to the opco rather than the group.

On its own merits the row reads well. it-novum positions explicitly as a business open source consultancy delivering DMS and workflow for the public sector, which is open-source posture stated as identity rather than inferred from a certification tier, in the vertical the thesis targets. That combination is what the posture screen is trying to find, which makes the parent-company overlap the main thing to reconcile rather than a reason to discount the lead. Provenance: Flowable Partner Finder, mined 2026-08-18, not imprint-swept.
